title: Gravitation
seo_title: Gravitation Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 9)
standard_text: Gravitation: Universal Law of Gravitation, Force of Gravitation of the earth (gravity), Acceleration due to Gravity; Mass and Weight; Free fall. Floatation: Thrust and Pressure. Archimedes’ Principle; Buoyancy.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 9: the universal law of gravitation, g, free fall, mass and weight, weight on the Moon, thrust and pressure, buoyancy, Archimedes' principle and relative density. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Every two objects attract each other: F = Gm₁m₂ ÷ d².
key_sub: W = mg; on the Moon weight is one-sixth.
body_html:
How to think about it

The gravitational force between two masses is F = Gm₁m₂ ÷ d², so doubling the distance makes it one-fourth. Near the Earth all objects fall with the same acceleration g ≈ 9.8 m/s², so the equations of motion apply with a = g. Weight is the force of gravity, W = mg; mass stays the same everywhere.

Thrust is a force at right angles to a surface; pressure = thrust ÷ area, in pascals. A fluid pushes up on an object (buoyancy), and by Archimedes' principle the upthrust equals the weight of fluid displaced. An object floats if its density is less than that of the liquid.

Example

Weight of 10 kg on the Earth?

W = 10 × 9.8

Answer: 98 N

Example

Distance doubled: force?

F ∝ 1/d²

Answer: one-fourth

Common mistakes

  • Saying mass changes on the Moon.
  • Using d instead of d² in the law of gravitation.
  • Thinking heavy objects fall faster in a vacuum.

faq.q: Why does a ship float although iron sinks?
faq.a: Its hollow shape displaces a weight of water equal to its own weight, so its average density is less than water's.

faq.q: What is the difference between g and G?
faq.a: g is the acceleration due to gravity (about 9.8 m/s² on the Earth); G is the universal constant 6.7 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², the same everywhere.

items.q: If the distance between two objects is doubled, what happens to the gravitational force?
The gravitational force between two objects is 120 N. What is the force if the distance between them is doubled?
The gravitational force between two objects is 120 N. What is the force if the distance between them is tripled?
Why are the blades of knives sharp?
c: a small area gives a large pressure, so they cut easily
items.e: Nails have pointed tips for the same reason.

items.q: What is free fall?
c: falling under the force of gravity alone
items.e: All objects fall with the same acceleration g.

items.q: Why does an iron nail sink in water but a cork floats?

iron is denser than water, while cork is less dense

items.q: The gravitational force between two objects is 20 N. What is the force if the mass of one object is made 4 times and the distance between them is doubled?
What is relative density?
c: the density of a substance divided by the density of water

items.q: What is buoyant force (upthrust)?
c: the upward force a liquid exerts on an object in it
items.e: It is why things seem lighter in water.

items.q: What is thrust?
c: the force acting on an object perpendicular to its surface

items.q: What does Archimedes' principle state?
c: an object in a fluid feels an upthrust equal to the weight of fluid it displaces
items.e: It is used to design ships.
